ListEmailImages — GET /email-images
UploadEmailImage — POST /email-images (multipart "file")

GetEmailAuthCheck validates SPF/DKIM/DMARC for a mailbox's sending domain on demand. Authentication alignment is a hard bulk-sender requirement and the most common silent deliverability failure, so this lets the user confirm their domain is set up correctly without leaving the dashboard.  Read-only: it reports what DNS says right now and leaves the mailbox's stored auth_state alone. Use RefreshEmailAuthCheck to record the verdict.

params.name: id
params.description: The mailbox id. The domain is derived from the mailbox address.

operations.doc: Write-scoped: recording the verdict is what lifts the cold-send and warmup gate, so a read-only key must not reach it.

GetEmailBehaviorPlan returns the workday this mailbox actually rolled for the current local date, plus how much of it is already spent. This is the read that answers "why is nothing sending right now" without anyone guessing. GET /emails/:id/behavior/plan
Human sending behaviour: the ranges the mailbox rolls its workday from, and the workday it rolled for today.

UpdateEmailBehavior applies a partial update to the profile. Omitted fields keep their stored value, so toggling `enabled` does not require resending every range.  Naturally idempotent: the body is the desired state, so a retry converges on the same profile and no Idempotency-Key is needed. PUT /emails/:id/behavior

UpdateEmailDirectTracking switches open/click tracking on this mailbox's hand-written unibox sends. Off by default, and deliberately per mailbox: a pixel belongs in a cold sequence more comfortably than in a one-to-one reply. PATCH /emails/:id/direct-tracking
The owner's hold on campaign sending. Bodyless and idempotent, so no Idempotency-Key.

RefreshEmailSendIdentity re-reads the mailbox's send-as addresses from the provider and stores them, optionally importing the provider's signature.  Retry-safe without an Idempotency-Key: it reads the provider's current state and writes exactly that, so repeating it converges on the same row. POST /emails/:id/identity/refresh

params.name: import_signature
params.description: Also replace the mailbox's stored signature with the one configured at the provider, for whichever identity the mailbox sends as. An empty signature at the provider changes nothing.

operations.doc: Which addresses the provider will let this mailbox send as, and where its signature came from. The refresh is the only half that calls the provider, and storing its answer is what a send-as choice is validated against, so it is write-scoped.
ReleaseEmail serves POST /emails/:id/release, putting a held or resting mailbox back into campaign rotation.
SendEmailFromAccount sends an email from a specific email account POST /emails/:id/send

params.name: in_reply_to
params.description: Message ids this email replies to.

params.name: thread_id
params.description: Thread id to attach the message to.

params.name: send_mode
params.description: SendMode picks the schedule strategy:   "instant" → enqueue immediately (default)   "smart"   → next gap in the per-mailbox scheduler   "scheduled" → use ScheduledAt verbatim (must be in the future)

params.name: scheduled_at
params.description: Required when send_mode is scheduled. Must be in the future.

operations.doc: GetEmailSync reports a mailbox's sync progress, fair-use status and folder settings.

params.name: skip_folders
params.description: Folder names as the server lists them. Case does not matter; each covers its subfolders. An empty list syncs every folder.

operations.doc: Write-scoped like the auth-check refresh: persisting the verdict is what routes real links through the custom host.

params.name: domain
params.description: The custom tracking subdomain (for example t.acme.com). Empty clears it.

operations.doc: SubmitWarmupAppeal lets a member who manages mailboxes appeal a warmup ban with a reason.

operations.doc: GetWarmupBanStatus returns whether a mailbox is blocked from warmup, why, and whether the owner can appeal. Powers the dashboard ban banner.
PauseWarmup pauses warmup without losing ramp progress; a later start continues from the same daily volume.
ResumeWarmup resumes a paused warmup, shifting the ramp anchor forward so progress continues where it left off.
StartWarmup enables (or resumes) warmup for a mailbox, preserving ramp progress when resuming from a paused state.
StopWarmup disables warmup entirely and clears ramp progress — a later start begins a fresh ramp. Distinct from PauseWarmup, which preserves progress.

params.name: signature_code
params.description: Treat the HTML signature as raw code.

params.name: send_as_email
params.description: SendAsEmail picks which verified provider alias the mailbox sends from. An empty string clears it back to the mailbox's own address; anything else has to be an address the provider reported as verified.

params.description: Percentage of warmup threads to reply to.

params.description: WarmupPlacement is "folder", "inbox" or "archive"; WarmupFolder names the destination for "folder" and is cleared back to the instance default by an empty string.

params.description: Folder (Gmail label) warmup mail is filed into when warmup_placement is "folder". Send an empty string to fall back to the instance default. No folder separators or control characters; 64 characters max.

params.description: WarmupRetentionDays is how long warmup mail is kept in the mailbox; 0 goes back to the instance setting.

params.description: Timezone is the mailbox's own IANA zone, which its sending behaviour and business-hours window are evaluated in. Empty means not configured, so only the campaign's window applies.

params.description: SaveToSent controls the Sent folder copy on SMTP/IMAP mailboxes. Turn it off when the submission server files its own copy, or the folder ends up with two of everything.

It is gated on the operational PermUseIntegrations / APIPermIntegrations (see routes.go) rather than the settings permission, so an operator can push without full settings access.  Retries are naturally safe: every provider upsert is keyed by email, so a repeated push converges rather than duplicating records — no Idempotency-Key bookkeeping is required. Per-record results are returned so the dashboard can report exactly which contacts synced.

params.description: Only seeds at these provider families, as the overview's panels[].families[].family lists them. The way to narrow a test on the instance and cloud panels, whose addresses are masked.

params.name: pace
params.description: spaced sends about 60 seconds apart; quick about 8 seconds apart, so a test sends in minutes.

params.name: max_credits
params.description: The most credits you agree to pay when the month's free tests on the instance panel are used up. A higher price, or none sent, is refused with placement_quota_exceeded, whose message names the price, and nothing is charged.

operations.doc: Plans and timezones are essentially public reference data — auth gates them only to avoid being scraped. Cheap to expose to keys.
AddSegmentToCampaign enrols the segment's current members as campaign leads.

params.name: campaign_id
params.description: The campaign to add them to

operations.doc: GetSegmentMemberModes reports the manual override of the given contacts.
SetSegmentMembers writes a manual include/exclude override (or clears it).

params.name: all
params.description: All switches the selection from the id list to Filters.

params.name: filters
params.description: Filters is the same search body /contacts/search takes, so the set resolved here is exactly the set the list was showing.

params.name: exclude
params.description: Exclude drops ids from the resolved set: the rows unticked after a select-all. Ignored unless All is set.

operations.doc: ListSegmentOverrides lists the contacts pinned into or out of a segment.
PreviewSegment counts the contacts an unsaved definition would match.

params.name: cursor
params.description: Opaque pagination cursor from the previous page's pagination.next_cursor.

params.name: q
params.description: Substring filter on the address or domain.

params.name: reason
params.description: Reason applies to every entry that does not carry its own.

params.name: color
params.description: Hex colour, `#rrggbb`. Omit to let the server pick from its palette.

params.name: id
params.description: The dead-letter record ID (the `id` field, not `task_id`).

params.name: user_id
params.description: The member's user id (must already belong to the organization).

operations.doc: DuplicateTemplate clones a template, appending " (copy)" to the name and placing it at the end of the org's list. POST /templates/:id/duplicate
RenderTemplate expands {{.Key}} placeholders in subject + body fields using a caller-supplied variable map. Used by Unibox to preview a reply before scheduling the send. POST /templates/:id/render
DeleteTemplate deletes a reply template DELETE /templates/:id
GetTemplate retrieves a reply template by ID GET /templates/:id
UpdateTemplate updates a reply template PATCH /templates/:id

The AI half of the same check. It spends the workspace's AI credits, so it takes the WRITE scope even though it writes no template: a read-only key must not be able to spend money. JWT members still need only view_campaigns, plus use_ai, which the second gate layers on as /generation does.
ReorderTemplates reassigns positions across the org's templates so they line up with the order in the request body. PATCH /templates/reorder

params.name: ids
params.description: Template IDs in their new order (1-indexed). IDs omitted are left untouched.

operations.doc: ScoreTemplateContent returns an advisory deliverability content score for a campaign template (subject + body) before it is sent. Advisory only — it never blocks sending — so the user gets content feedback on the mail that actually reaches prospects, which warmup-only linting never covered.
ListTemplates lists all reply templates for the organization, optionally filtered by `?q=` against name and subject. GET /templates

params.name: q
params.description: Optional case-insensitive search over name and subject.

operations.doc: CreateTemplate creates a new reply template POST /templates
Keep /:id last — gin treats it as a catch-all so any fixed-name routes (above) must register first.

ApproveAgentDraft — POST /unibox/agent-drafts/:id/approve Sends the draft (optionally with an edited body) through the normal reply path and marks it approved. The status flip is claimed BEFORE sending so two approvals can never double-send.
DiscardAgentDraft — POST /unibox/agent-drafts/:id/discard Dismisses a pending draft without sending.

Inbox agent drafts (M10): review the pending drafts the agent suggested on inbound human replies, then approve-and-send or discard. Approve reuses the normal reply send path. Registered before /:id so the fixed path wins over the catch-all.
Compose: send a brand-new outbound email. The candidates endpoint scores mailboxes for a recipient (affinity, budget, auth) so the picker and Auto mode can explain their choice.
Grounded AI draft for compose: contact + history + voice profile context; may return a clarifying question instead of a draft. Charges credits, never sends.
UniboxCompose sends a brand-new outbound email (not a reply), with automatic mailbox selection. The send service refuses a suppressed recipient. POST /unibox/compose

params.name: email_account_id
params.description: EmailAccountID empty (or "auto") lets the backend pick the best mailbox for the first recipient.

params.name: from_tag_id
params.description: FromTagID scopes the automatic pick to mailboxes carrying this tag ("Auto within a tag"). Ignored when EmailAccountID is explicit.

operations.doc: GetUnseenCount gets the count of unseen emails GET /unibox/count

params.name: email_id
params.description: Optional mailbox UUID to count unread for a single mailbox.

operations.doc: DeleteComposeDraft — DELETE /unibox/drafts/:id
UpsertComposeDraft — PUT /unibox/drafts/:id
Autosaved compose drafts (per-user; client-generated ids make the PUT idempotent for debounced autosave).

UniboxMoveFolder re-files messages (Archive = archive, Delete = trash, Move to inbox = inbox). Org-scoped like /seen: the inbox is shared, so any member with unibox access may file it. Naturally idempotent, so no Idempotency-Key: the body names the destination, not a delta. PATCH /unibox/folder

params.name: thread_ids
params.description: ThreadIDs files whole conversations. A row in the list knows its thread but not the ids inside it, and filing half a conversation leaves it in the view it was filed out of. Each entry is a thread id, or a message id for mail that never got one.

params.name: folder
params.description: Destination folder. Anything else is a `400`.

operations.doc: GetUniboxOverview rolls up unread/today/week/snoozed/awaiting plus per-mailbox and per-tag counts in one call. The dashboard's scope rail and metric strip share this response. GET /unibox/overview
AI reply draft: context-grounded, charges credits, never sends.
UniboxReply schedules a reply or forward email from Unibox. POST /unibox/reply

params.name: email_account_id
params.description: UUID of the sending mailbox. Any active mailbox in the organization; it does not have to be the one holding the thread.

params.name: thread_id
params.description: The conversation being answered. Resolves In-Reply-To when that is omitted, and is used as the provider thread only by a mailbox holding a message in it.

params.name: scheduled_at
params.description: Required when `send_mode` is `scheduled`; must be in the future.

params.name: forward_message_id
params.description: ForwardMessageID makes the send a forward of that stored message, which goes out under the body and signature.

operations.doc: CancelUniboxScheduled cancels a pending scheduled send. DB-only: we mark the task cancelled and let the queued Cloud Task fire as a no-op (the task handler short-circuits on non-pending statuses). DELETE /unibox/scheduled/:task_id

params.name: task_id
params.description: UUID of the scheduled task to cancel.

operations.doc: Scheduled-sends review + cancel. DELETE is DB-only — we don't pay Cloud Tasks to delete the queued task; the handler short-circuits on cancelled status when it fires.

params.name: thread_id
params.description: Restrict to scheduled sends queued into one thread.

params.name: thread_ids
params.description: ThreadIDs marks whole conversations, so a caller holding a list row does not have to fetch the thread to learn its message ids. Each entry is a thread id, or a message id for mail that never got one.

params.name: folder
params.description: Folder, when set, marks every unread message in that folder for the whole workspace instead of the explicit id list.

params.name: seen
params.description: `true` marks as read, `false` marks as unread.

operations.doc: DeleteUniboxSnooze un-snoozes a thread immediately. Idempotent — deleting a snooze that doesn't exist still returns 204. DELETE /unibox/snooze

params.name: thread_id
params.description: The thread to un-snooze, or a comma-separated list of them.

operations.doc: CreateUniboxSnooze hides conversations until snoozed_until passes. Upsert semantics: a second call on the same thread updates the time. A request naming one thread answers with that row, as it always has; one naming several answers with `data`. POST /unibox/snooze

params.name: thread_ids
params.description: ThreadIDs snoozes a whole selection in one call. Either field will do; naming both snoozes the union.

params.name: snoozed_until
params.description: RFC 3339 timestamp to un-hide the thread.

operations.doc: Snoozes — POST/DELETE on a thread, GET lists active ones.
Conversation labels — read the set on a thread, or replace it wholesale (idempotent PUT). Registered before /:id so the fixed path wins over the catch-all.

params.name: thread_id
params.description: The thread to read labels for. Also accepted as `id`.

operations.doc: SetUniboxThreadLabels replaces the full conversation-label set on a thread. Idempotent (PUT semantics): the body's category_ids is the desired set, so retries are naturally safe. Only the workspace's own categories are attached. PUT /unibox/thread/labels

params.name: category_ids
params.description: Full desired set of category UUIDs. An empty array clears all labels.

params.name: email_id
params.description: Optional mailbox UUID to scope the thread to one mailbox. Also accepted as `email`.

params.name: thread_id
params.description: The thread to read. Also accepted as `id`.

params.name: cursor
params.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response.

params.name: limit
params.description: Page size, clamped to the server min/max.

params.name: address
params.description: Conversations with this address, either direction

params.name: folder
params.description: Canonical folder scope. Omit for every working folder: `spam`, `trash` and `archive` stay out.

params.name: include_archived
params.description: `true` puts archived conversations back into the result, which is what the All mail view does. Ignored when `folder` is set.

params.name: unseen
params.description: `true` returns only threads with unread messages.

params.name: snoozed
params.description: `true` returns only snoozed threads. Omit to exclude snoozed threads.

params.name: awaiting_reply
params.description: `true` returns only threads whose latest message was sent by one of your mailboxes.

params.name: email_id
params.description: Restrict to a single mailbox by UUID.

params.name: email_ids
params.description: Comma-separated mailbox UUIDs. A thread matches if it landed in any of them.

params.name: automated
params.description: `true` returns only conversations no person wrote in (security alerts, notifications, bounces, auto-replies), as judged by automatic inbox tagging. `false` leaves them out, which is how the dashboard's Inbox reads. Omit for both.

params.name: category_ids
params.description: Comma-separated conversation-label UUIDs. A thread matches if it carries any of them.

operations.doc: DeleteWarmupRoutingRule removes a rule by ID.
UpdateWarmupRoutingRule updates a rule by ID.

params.name: priority
params.description: Evaluation order, ascending. Lower runs first.

params.name: sender_match_value
params.description: Required unless sender_match_type is any. Domain (acme.com), TLD (com), or provider bucket (google, microsoft, yahoo, apple, proton, zoho, custom).

params.name: recipient_match_value
params.description: Required unless recipient_match_type is any. Same value forms as the sender side.

params.name: weight
params.description: Selection weight, must be >= 0. Above 1 prefers the pairing, below 1 avoids it, and exactly 0 excludes it even when no other partner is available.

operations.doc: ListWarmupRoutingRules returns every rule for the caller's organization, ordered by priority (ascending — first to evaluate).
CreateWarmupRoutingRule creates a new rule for the caller's organization.

params.name: priority
params.description: Evaluation order, ascending. Lower runs first.

params.name: sender_match_value
params.description: Required unless sender_match_type is any. Domain (acme.com), TLD (com), or provider bucket (google, microsoft, yahoo, apple, proton, zoho, custom).

params.name: recipient_match_value
params.description: Required unless recipient_match_type is any. Same value forms as the sender side.

params.name: weight
params.description: Selection weight, must be >= 0. Above 1 prefers the pairing, below 1 avoids it, and exactly 0 excludes it even when no other partner is available.

operations.doc: ListWebhookDeliveries returns recent delivery attempts (org-wide, or for one endpoint via ?endpoint_id=), filterable by status/event_type, with opaque cursor pagination.  GET /webhooks/deliveries  and  GET /webhooks/:id/deliveries

params.name: id
params.description: The endpoint id whose deliveries to list.

params.name: limit
params.description: Max rows to return. Between 1 and 200. Defaults to 50. Out-of-range values return 400.

operations.doc: RotateWebhookSecret issues a new signing secret and returns it once. Existing in-flight deliveries continue to use the old secret until they settle; new deliveries use the new one.

VerifyWebhookEndpoint (re)sends the signed challenge / test request to the endpoint so it can prove it accepts our deliveries. Doubles as "send a test event": a 2xx verifies the endpoint and starts the event stream.  POST /webhooks/:id/verify
DeleteWebhookEndpoint deletes a subscription and cascades to its delivery history.
UpdateWebhookEndpoint updates a subscription. The secret is not changed here — use POST /webhooks/:id/rotate-secret to rotate it. Changing the URL host re-arms ownership verification.

params.name: url
params.description: HTTPS URL that will receive POST callbacks. Must be publicly routable.

params.name: description
params.description: Free-text label for your own reference.

params.name: event_types
params.description: Event names to subscribe to. Each must be a known type. An empty or omitted array subscribes to all events. On update this overwrites the existing filter (not merged).

params.name: enabled
params.description: Whether the endpoint is active. Defaults to true.

operations.doc: RedeliverWebhookDelivery re-queues an existing delivery (same event id) for a fresh attempt cycle.  POST /webhooks/deliveries/:deliveryId/redeliver

ListWebhookDeliveries returns recent delivery attempts (org-wide, or for one endpoint via ?endpoint_id=), filterable by status/event_type, with opaque cursor pagination.  GET /webhooks/deliveries  and  GET /webhooks/:id/deliveries
Discovery + cross-endpoint views (static paths; sit beside :id).
ListWebhookDrops surfaces events the dispatch throttle dropped (rate-limiting visibility), rolled up by day for the last 30 days.  GET /webhooks/throttle-drops
ListWebhookEndpoints returns every endpoint configured for the caller's organization. Secrets are not included.

CreateWebhookEndpoint creates a new subscription. The response includes the signing secret — this is the only time it is returned, so clients must capture it. Subsequent reads return the endpoint without the secret.  When the caller authenticated with an OAuth access token, the endpoint is bound to that app and its URL host must fall within the app's allowed webhook domains.

params.name: url
params.description: HTTPS URL that will receive POST callbacks. Must be publicly routable.

params.name: description
params.description: Free-text label for your own reference.

params.name: event_types
params.description: Event names to subscribe to. Each must be a known type. An empty or omitted array subscribes to all events. On update this overwrites the existing filter (not merged).

params.name: enabled
